To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new interpair optimization method that can be applied to all-pairs sequence comparisons and that we achieved 2.1 times speed-up on a single GPU for the all-pair comparisons of sequences from the same species.

our interpair pruning and optimization method accelerates the all-pairs local sequence alignment of sequences from the same species by pruning 73 % of all matrix cells on two graphics processing units (GPU).
interpair optimization for the Smith-Wwaterman algorithm is effective for accelerating the all-pair comparison of the sequences from the same species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following points.
the acceleration of the Smith-Watermann algorithm for the all-pair comparison of base sequences using interpair optimization.

the following: (1) the development of an interpair block pruning method for the Smith–Waterman algorithm, (2) the implementation of the Smith–Water-man algorithm on the GPU, and (3) the evaluation of the acceleration achieved using the Smith–Water-mann algorithm with the proposed interpair block pruning for the all-pair comparison of base sequences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is useful for the all-pair comparisons of base sequences of the same genome, but is less effective for the comparison between genomes of different species.
our interpair block pruning algorithm is useful in accelerating applications that require optimal alignment scores for same-species sequences.
our method is useful for the all-pair comparisons of base sequences of the same or similar species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the acceleration of the all-pairs sequence comparison is possible by using the interpair pruning method, which is effective when the sequences of the species to be compared are highly similar to one another.
we achieved 1.2x acceleration compared with the intrapair optimization method, and we also realized the first all-pair comparison of 1.5 billion base sequences on two GPUs.
we have achieved a speedup of 1.5 times for the all-pair comparison of the same species compared with a previous method that uses intrapair pruning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interpair optimization of the Smith-Watermen algorithm can be accelerated using GPUs.
the interpair optimization method is more efficient than the intrapairs pruning method for the all-pair comparisons of base sequences of the same organism.

interpair optimization can be used for accelerating the first phase of Smith-Waterman, where our method significantly improves the initial lower bound, and that the method is useful in applications that require optimal alignment scores for the same sequences.
